title: The generic fibre of a domain over a domain is an irreducible spectrum
statement: Let $A$ be an integral domain with field of fractions $K$, and let $A\to C$ be a ring map into an integral domain $C$ such that every nonzero $a\in A$ has nonzero image in $C$. Let $S\subset C$ be the image of $A\setminus\{0\}$, a multiplicative subset not containing $0$. Then $K\otimes_AC$ is a localization $S^{-1}C$ of $C$ at $S$; it is an integral domain; and its spectrum $\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_AC)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is nonempty and irreducible, in particular connected [def-weil-connected-scheme].

source.place: Stacks Project, Algebra: localization commutes with tensor products, Lemma (Tag 00DK); a localization of a domain at a multiplicative set not containing 0 is a domain (Section Tag 00CM); Spec of a domain is irreducible with generic point (0), Lemma (Tag 00ES); an irreducible space is connected (Topology, Section Tag 004U, text after Definition topology-definition-irreducible-components: "An irreducible space is obviously connected")
